tier_rationale: No intentional-radiator FCC grant exists for this model while VIOFO holds grants for every sibling model that has a radio, and the manufacturer spec table states Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are not supported.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes, because there is nothing to unplug. The camera has no Wi-Fi and no Bluetooth, so there is no app, no account, and no pairing step. You put a microSD card in, plug it into 12V, and it records in a loop. Everything is configured on the 2-inch screen with four buttons.

repairability.notes: Capacitor-based rather than battery-based, which removes the usual dashcam failure mode of a swollen lithium cell.

sources.supports: Manufacturer specification table states 'Wi-Fi: Not supported' and 'Bluetooth: Not supported'. GPS logger built in. Listed at $139.99.

No intentional-radiator grant for the A119 V3. VIOFO holds grants for WR1 (2AMBWWR1), VS1 (2AMBWVS1) and A139 (2AMBWA139), all covering Wi-Fi or Bluetooth — so the absence of a grant for this model is meaningful rather than an unfiled gap.

Firmware is updated by copying a .bin file to the root of the microSD card and power-cycling the camera. There is no over-the-air path, so the vendor cannot change this device's behaviour after purchase.

notes: The reference case for D0 in this catalog: a mainstream, currently-sold consumer device with no radio at all. Sibling models in the same product line do have Wi-Fi, so this is a deliberate product decision rather than an old design.
